title: Ibragimov's CLT: the sharp polynomial-mixing threshold
content:
The module docstring states the open question and its sharp answer. Given a stationary $\alpha$-mixing sequence $\{X_n\}$ with $E[X_1]=0$, $E[|X_1|^{2+\delta}]<\infty$ for some $\delta>0$, and mixing coefficients decaying at the *polynomial* rate $\alpha(n)\le C\,n^{-r}$, the sharp threshold for the CLT is $r>(2+\delta)/\delta$: exactly at this threshold the Ibragimov (1962) covariance-summability condition $\sum_n\alpha(n)^{\delta/(2+\delta)}<\infty$ holds, so the Bernstein-blocks argument delivers $S_n/\sqrt n\to_d\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)$.

This file has grown well past its original S2 orient-scaffold: it now carries a nearly complete, axiom-free *Davydov covariance-inequality development* — the $\alpha$-mixing coefficient basic facts (S4/S5), the indicator base case (S5b), the simple-function bilinear step (S16/S17/S20), covariance translation-invariance (S19), the full layer-cake machinery reducing the $L^p$ density step to super-level indicators (S21–S25), and the bounded-variable Davydov estimate (S26/S27). Two `sorry`s remain and are stated honestly: `davydov_covariance_inequality` (the general $L^p$ bound, whose only missing piece is the truncation + Hölder amplification of the bounded estimate) and `mixing_clt_ibragimov` (the headline CLT, deferred to the S6+ Bernstein-block + Lindeberg phase). Everything feeding those two statements is fully verified with 0 axioms.
mathContext: Sharp threshold: $r > \dfrac{2+\delta}{\delta}$. Equivalently $\dfrac{r\,\delta}{2+\delta} > 1$, the $p$-series exponent controlling $\sum_n \alpha(n)^{\delta/(2+\delta)} = \sum_n n^{-r\delta/(2+\delta)}$.

title: Mathlib + parent-file imports
content: The imports assemble the four analytic pillars of the Davydov development plus the parent's $\alpha$-mixing API. `MeasureTheory.Function.LpSpace.Basic` supplies `MemLp`/`eLpNorm` for the $(2+\delta)$-moment hypotheses; `MeasureTheory.Integral.Bochner.Set` provides the set-integral (`setIntegral`, `Measure.restrict`) machinery used throughout the layer-cake step; `MeasureTheory.Integral.Layercake` is the crucial one — it provides `Integrable.integral_eq_integral_meas_lt`, the Cavalieri identity from which every survival-function representation is derived; `Analysis.PSeries` gives `Real.summable_nat_rpow`, the $\zeta$-function summability fact; and `Probability.IdentDistrib` provides the marginal-stationarity predicate. The decisive dependency is `Proofs.CentralLimitTheoremOQ02`, the parent file that introduces `alphaMixingCoeff`, `AlphaMixingSequence`, and `longRunVariance` — Mathlib has no native $\alpha$-mixing API, so the parent supplies it (and this file even closes the parent's `alphaMixingCoeff_nonneg` TODO).
mathContext: Open namespaces: `MeasureTheory`, `ProbabilityTheory`, `Filter`, `Real`, `Topology`. These unify Bochner integration, probability measures, sequential limits, real-valued `rpow`, and `𝓝`-convergence in one tactic context.

title: Marginal stationarity predicate
content: `Stationary μ X` asserts that every $X_k$ has the same marginal distribution as $X_0$ under $\mu$, encoded with Mathlib's `IdentDistrib`. This is the weakest stationarity slice — exactly what the long-run-variance computation needs at the level of one-dimensional integrals ($E[X_k]=E[X_0]$, $\|X_k\|_{2+\delta}=\|X_0\|_{2+\delta}$; the latter is `stationary_eLpNorm_eq` downstream). Full joint (finite-tuple) stationarity is the natural strengthening the S6 Bernstein-block argument will need and is deferred. Using `IdentDistrib` keeps the predicate Mathlib-native so it composes with `Integrable.congr`, `MemLp.congr`, and `eLpNorm` congruence lemmas.
mathContext: $\mathrm{Stationary}(\mu, X)\iff \forall k,\; X_k \stackrel{d}{=} X_0\text{ under }\mu$.

title: Polynomial α-mixing rate
content: `PolynomialMixingRate α C r` says the numerical mixing bound decays polynomially: $\alpha(n)\le C\,n^{-r}$ for $n\ge 1$, with $C>0$, $r>0$. The polynomial rate is the most-studied and most delicate case in the mixing-CLT literature: exponential mixing $\alpha(n)\le Ce^{-rn}$ makes the covariance sum trivially convergent (the CLT comes for free), whereas polynomial mixing exhibits the *sharp* dependence on the moment exponent $\delta$ that this entry quantifies — the whole point of the $r>(2+\delta)/\delta$ threshold.
mathContext: $\mathrm{PolynomialMixingRate}(\alpha, C, r) := C > 0 \wedge r > 0 \wedge \forall n\ge 1,\; \alpha(n) \le C\,n^{-r}$.

title: Uniform (2+δ)-th moment bound
content: `MomentBound2δ μ X δ` asserts every $X_k\in L^{2+\delta}(\mu)$, i.e. $E[|X_k|^{2+\delta}]<\infty$. The exponent $2+\delta$ with $\delta>0$ is sharp: it cannot be relaxed to $\delta=0$ (bare second moments) without breaking both the Lindeberg condition in the Bernstein-block proof *and* the Davydov exponent $(p-2)/p=\delta/(2+\delta)$ that must be positive for the covariance bound to decay. The encoding via `MemLp (X k) (ENNReal.ofReal (2+δ)) μ` is Mathlib-native, carrying both snorm-finiteness and the strong measurability needed by every downstream integration.
mathContext: $\mathrm{MomentBound2\delta}(\mu, X, \delta)\iff \forall k,\; X_k \in L^{2+\delta}(\mu) \iff \forall k,\; \int |X_k|^{2+\delta}\,d\mu < \infty$.

title: IbragimovHypotheses: the bundled CLT premise
content:
`IbragimovHypotheses` packages the theorem's assumptions into one argument. Its fields are: stationarity; per-index integrability and mean-zero; the moment exponent `delta_pos` and the `moment_bound`; a numerical mixing coefficient `alpha : ℕ → ℝ` with `alpha_nonneg`; the past/future $\sigma$-algebra families `pastSigma`, `futureSigma` together with `past_measurable`/`future_measurable` (each $X_k$ is adapted) and `past_le`/`future_le` (each is a genuine sub-$\sigma$-algebra of the ambient space — needed so that level sets $\{X>t\}$ are ambient-measurable at the Davydov call site); the bridge `alpha_bound` witnessing that the parent's abstract `alphaMixingCoeff` is dominated by the numerical `alpha`; the decay assertion `poly_rate`; and the sharp-threshold field `rate_admissible : r > (2+δ)/δ`.

**Axiom-integrity note.** These fields ARE the mathematical assumptions of the CLT — the structure encodes the hypotheses rather than asserting stand-alone axioms, so `axiomCount = 0` is correct, while `status: axiomatized` reflects the two remaining `sorry`s (`davydov_covariance_inequality`, `mixing_clt_ibragimov`). Restructuring premises into a structure does not reduce the assumption count; it only bundles them.

**The sharp-threshold field.** The last field `rate_admissible : r > (2+δ)/δ` carries the entire *sharpness* content of Ibragimov's theorem. Above this threshold the Bernstein-block proof carries through; below it the CLT can fail (explicit counterexamples: Bradley, *Introduction to Strong Mixing Conditions*, Vol. III). The exponent $(2+\delta)/\delta$ is the unique value at which Davydov's covariance bound, the moment hypothesis, and the variance-series summability all become simultaneously feasible — precisely where $\frac{r\delta}{2+\delta}$ crosses $1$, the boundary of $p$-series convergence.
mathContext: $\mathrm{IbragimovHypotheses}(\mu, X, \delta, C, r)$: $X$ stationary, integrable, mean-zero, $\delta>0$, $X\in L^{2+\delta}$, past/future $\sigma$-algebras $\mathcal F_k^-,\mathcal F_{k+n}^+$ with $\alpha\text{-coeff}(\mathcal F_k^-,\mathcal F_{k+n}^+)\le\alpha(n)$, $\alpha(n)\le C n^{-r}$, and $r>(2+\delta)/\delta$.

title: Polynomial summability (the ζ-function fact)
content: `polynomial_summable_of_exponent_gt_one s hs` proves $\sum_n n^{-s}<\infty$ for $s>1$ in a single line: `Real.summable_nat_rpow.mpr (by linarith)`. Mathlib's `Real.summable_nat_rpow` characterises `Summable (fun n => (n:ℝ) ^ p)` as `p < -1`; instantiating $p=-s$ turns $s>1$ into $-s<-1$, which `linarith` discharges. This is the analytic engine behind the sharp threshold — everything else in Part II is bookkeeping that reduces the covariance series to this $p$-series.
mathContext: $\sum_{n=1}^\infty n^{-s} < \infty \iff s > 1$ (Euler's $\zeta$ fact). Encoded as `Summable (fun n => (n:ℝ) ^ (-s))` via `Real.summable_nat_rpow` at exponent $-s < -1$.

title: Sharp-threshold summability corollary
content: `ibragimov_threshold_summable` is the fully-proven corollary that actually *uses* the threshold: from $\delta>0$ and $r>(2+\delta)/\delta$ it deduces $\sum_n n^{-r\delta/(2+\delta)}<\infty$. The proof reduces to `polynomial_summable_of_exponent_gt_one` once the algebra $\frac{r\delta}{2+\delta}>1$ is verified: multiply $r>(2+\delta)/\delta$ by $\delta>0$ (via `mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right` + `div_mul_cancel₀`) to get $r\delta>2+\delta$, then divide by $2+\delta>0$ using `lt_div_iff₀`. This is the exponent that reappears as `polynomial_mixing_summable`, the summable envelope for the long-run-variance series.
mathContext: $r > (2+\delta)/\delta$ and $\delta > 0 \Rightarrow \frac{r\delta}{2+\delta} > 1$, hence $\sum_n n^{-r\delta/(2+\delta)}$ converges.

title: Truncation tail second-moment bound (S18)
content: Part II-bis supplies the truncation estimates that both the Lindeberg condition (S9) and the $L^p$ density step inside Davydov's inequality rely on. `sq_le_rpow_of_large` is the pointwise seed: on the large-values region $T<|x|$, with $p\ge 2$, one has $x^2\le T^{-\delta}|x|^{2+\delta}$ (raising $|x|/T>1$ to the power $\delta=p-2$). Integrating this bound gives `truncation_tail_sq_le`: the second moment of a variable restricted to its tail $\{|X|>T\}$ is controlled by $T^{-\delta}$ times its $(2+\delta)$-th moment. Both are fully verified, 0-axiom, and quantify how truncation error shrinks as the cutoff $T\to\infty$ — the mechanism that trades the $(2+\delta)$-moment hypothesis for uniform integrability of the squared truncations.
mathContext: Pointwise on $\{T<|x|\}$: $x^2 = |x|^{2+\delta}\,|x|^{-\delta} \le |x|^{2+\delta}\,T^{-\delta}$. Integrated: $\int_{\{|X|>T\}} X^2 \le T^{-\delta}\,E[|X|^{2+\delta}]$.

title: α-mixing coefficient basic facts (S4/S5)
content: Part III proves the order-theoretic facts about the parent's `alphaMixingCoeff` — a 4-fold nested supremum $\sup_{A}\sup_{B}|\mu(A\cap B)-\mu(A)\mu(B)|$ over measurable pairs. `indicator_cov_le_one` is the uniform $[0,1]$ envelope: every indicator-covariance term is $\le 1$, the `BddAbove` witness that makes each `ciSup` well-behaved. From it, `alphaMixingCoeff_le_one` bounds the whole nested sup by $1$, and `alphaMixingCoeff_nonneg` shows $0\le\alpha(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$ via `Real.iSup_nonneg` layer-by-layer — the latter closes a TODO the parent file `CentralLimitTheoremOQ02.lean` had left open at line 444 ('omitted due to nested ciSup elaboration complexity'). All three are verified, 0-axiom, and are named ingredients (1)–(2) of the Davydov structural decomposition.
mathContext: $\alpha(\mathcal F,\mathcal G) = \sup_{A\in\mathcal F}\sup_{B\in\mathcal G}\bigl|\mu(A\cap B) - \mu(A)\mu(B)\bigr|$, with $0\le\alpha\le 1$ for a probability measure.

title: Davydov's indicator base case (S5b)
content: `davydov_indicator_bound` is the indicator base case of Davydov's inequality and named ingredient (3) of its decomposition: for measurable sets $A\in\sigma\mathrm{Pair}\,0$, $B\in\sigma\mathrm{Pair}\,1$, the indicator covariance is bounded by the mixing coefficient, $|\mu(A\cap B)_{\mathbb R} - \mu(A)_{\mathbb R}\mu(B)_{\mathbb R}|\le\alpha(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$. This is literally the *defining* inequality of `alphaMixingCoeff`, packaged for direct use: the proof peels the four nested $\bigsqcup$ layers — `le_ciSup_of_le` for the two `Set Ω` layers (with `BddAbove` witnesses uniformly from `indicator_cov_le_one`) and `ciSup_pos` for the two `Prop` layers. $\sigma$-algebras are passed in the function form `σPair : Fin 2 → MeasurableSpace Ω`, dodging a Lean 4 typeclass-synthesis clash when both a `MeasurableSpace Ω` argument and the ambient instance are in scope. Verified, 0-axiom; it is the atom every simple-function and layer-cake step ultimately reduces to.
mathContext: $|\,\mu(A\cap B).\mathrm{toReal} - \mu(A).\mathrm{toReal}\cdot\mu(B).\mathrm{toReal}\,| \le \alpha(\sigma\mathrm{Pair}\,0,\ \sigma\mathrm{Pair}\,1)$ for $A,B$ measurable in the respective sub-σ-algebras.

title: From indicators to scaled indicators (Part IV)
content: Part IV bridges the abstract mixing bound into the explicit covariance form the density step needs. `indicator_pair_covariance_eq` is the algebraic identity $\int \mathbf 1_A\cdot\mathbf 1_B\,d\mu = \mu(A\cap B)$ plus the marginal factorization, so covariance-of-indicators equals `davydov_indicator_bound`'s left-hand side. Composing the two gives `indicator_covariance_le_alpha`: $|\mathrm{Cov}(\mathbf 1_A,\mathbf 1_B)|\le\alpha(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$ in the integral form (a 3-line proof through `Measure.real_def`). Finally `scaled_indicator_covariance_le_alpha` promotes it to arbitrary real scalars, $|\mathrm{Cov}(a\mathbf 1_A, b\mathbf 1_B)|\le|a||b|\,\alpha(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$ — the single-cell building block of the simple-function step. All verified, 0-axiom.
mathContext: $\int \mathbf 1_A\mathbf 1_B = \mu(A\cap B)$; hence $|\mathrm{Cov}(a\mathbf 1_A, b\mathbf 1_B)| = |a|\,|b|\,|\mu(A\cap B)-\mu(A)\mu(B)| \le |a|\,|b|\,\alpha(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$.

title: Simple-function Davydov bound (S17/S20)
content: `finset_indicator_covariance_le_alpha` lifts the single-cell bound to a pair of simple functions $f=\sum_i a_i\mathbf 1_{A_i}$ ($\sigma\mathrm{Pair}\,0$-measurable) and $g=\sum_j b_j\mathbf 1_{B_j}$ ($\sigma\mathrm{Pair}\,1$-measurable): $|\mathrm{Cov}(f,g)|\le(\sum_i|a_i|)(\sum_j|b_j|)\,\alpha(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$. Covariance is bilinear, so both the joint integral and the product of marginals distribute over the double sum (`Finset.sum_mul_sum`, `integral_finset_sum`), and two applications of `Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs` plus the S16 per-cell bound collect the constant. Its companions `finset_indicator_covariance_le_alpha_of_nonneg` (nonnegative coefficients) and `telescoping_layer_covariance_le_alpha` specialize this to the layer-cake decomposition. Together they discharge the *algebraic* content of the $L^p$ density step — every $\sigma\mathrm{Pair}$-measurable simple function is exactly such a finite indicator combination — leaving only the analytic residue (truncation + Hölder) for the main sorry. Verified, 0-axiom.
mathContext: $\bigl|\mathrm{Cov}\bigl(\textstyle\sum_i a_i\mathbf 1_{A_i},\ \sum_j b_j\mathbf 1_{B_j}\bigr)\bigr| \le \bigl(\sum_i|a_i|\bigr)\bigl(\sum_j|b_j|\bigr)\,\alpha(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$.

title: Covariance translation-invariance (S19)
content: `covariance_add_const_left` and `covariance_add_const_right` prove $\mathrm{Cov}(f+c,g)=\mathrm{Cov}(f,g)$ and $\mathrm{Cov}(f,g+c)=\mathrm{Cov}(f,g)$ in the explicit $\int f g - (\int f)(\int g)$ form (under integrability of $f$, $g$, $fg$ on a probability measure). These are the algebraic reduction the Davydov density step uses to replace a *signed* bounded $f\in[m,M]$ by the *nonnegative* shift $f-m\in[0,M-m]$ — the form the layer-cake / super-level indicator decomposition requires (a super-level set $\{f>t\}$ only sweeps out $f$ cleanly when $f\ge 0$). Pure Bochner linearity: `integral_add` + `integral_const_mul` on the joint integral, $\int c\,d\mu=c$ on the marginal. Verified, 0-axiom.
mathContext: $\mathrm{Cov}(f+c, g) = \mathrm{Cov}(f, g)$; used to shift $f\in[m,M]$ to $f-m\in[0,M-m]$ so the super-level indicators $\mathbf 1_{\{f-m>t\}}$ cover $[0,M-m]$.

title: Layer-cake primitives (S21/S22)
content: This section builds the Cavalieri / layer-cake toolkit that expresses a bounded nonnegative variable through its super-level indicators. `layer_cake_pointwise` is the pointwise seed $\int_0^M \mathbf 1_{\{t<x\}}\,dt = x$ for $0\le x\le M$, with `layer_cake_repr` its representation orientation and `layer_cake_pointwise_prod` its bivariate product form $x\,y=\int_0^M\!\int_0^N \mathbf 1_{\{s<x\}}\mathbf 1_{\{t<y\}}$. `superlevel_setOf_measurable` records that $\{\omega : t<X(\omega)\}$ is sub-$\sigma$-measurable when $X$ is — the hook that feeds super-level indicators back into `indicator_covariance_le_alpha`. Integrating these against $\mu$, `mean_eq_survival_lt_Ioc` gives the bounded strict-$<$ Cavalieri form $\int f = \int_{(0,M]}\mu\{t<f\}\,dt$ (derived from Mathlib's `Integrable.integral_eq_integral_meas_lt` by killing the survival tail beyond $M$), and `mean_prod_eq_double_survival_lt_Ioc` gives the factorized product-of-marginals half of the covariance layer cake. All verified, 0-axiom.
mathContext: $\int_0^M \mathbf 1_{\{t<x\}}\,dt = x$ ($0\le x\le M$); integrated, $\int f = \int_{(0,M]} \mu\{t<f\}\,dt$ and $(\int f)(\int g) = \int_{(0,M]}\!\int_{(0,N]} \mu\{t<f\}\,\mu\{s<g\}$.

title: Joint bivariate layer cake (S23)
content: `mean_mul_eq_double_joint_survival_lt_Ioc` supplies the genuinely bivariate term of the covariance layer cake: $\int f g = \int_{(0,M]}\!\int_{(0,N]} \mu\{t<f \wedge s<g\}\,ds\,dt$ for measurable integrable $0\le f\le M$, $0\le g\le N$. The inner $s$-integral collapses *without* a product-measure Fubini: at fixed $t$, $\{t<f\wedge s<g\}=\{s<g\}\cap\{t<f\}$, so its survival is $(\mu\!\restriction\!\{t<f\})\{s<g\}$, and `mean_eq_survival_lt_Ioc` on the finite measure $\mu\!\restriction\!\{t<f\}$ rewrites it to $\int_{\{t<f\}} g$. The remaining single $t$-integral is swapped against $\omega$ by `integral_integral_swap` (the integrand $(\omega,t)\mapsto g(\omega)\mathbf 1_{\{t<f\}}$ is dominated by $\|g\|$ on the finite window $(0,M]$), collapsing via `layer_cake_pointwise_Ioc` to $\int g f$. Subtracting the marginal half yields the full representation $\mathrm{Cov}(f,g)=\int\!\int \mathrm{Cov}(\mathbf 1_{\{f>t\}},\mathbf 1_{\{g>s\}})\,ds\,dt$. Verified, 0-axiom.
mathContext: $\int f\,g\ =\ \int_{(0,M]}\!\!\int_{(0,N]} \mu\{t<f \wedge s<g\}\ ds\,dt$, the joint term of $\mathrm{Cov}(f,g)=\int\!\int\mathrm{Cov}(\mathbf 1_{\{f>t\}},\mathbf 1_{\{g>s\}})$.

title: Covariance as a double survival integral (S24/S25)
content: `covariance_eq_double_survival_covariance` assembles the marginal (S22) and joint (S23) halves into the covariance layer-cake representation: for bounded $0\le f\le M$, $0\le g\le N$, $\mathrm{Cov}(f,g)=\int_{(0,M]}\!\int_{(0,N]}\bigl(\mu\{t<f\wedge s<g\}-\mu\{t<f\}\mu\{s<g\}\bigr)\,ds\,dt$, with `survival_lt_integrableOn_Ioc` supplying the integrability atom. Then `survival_covariance_integrand_le_alpha` bounds the integrand uniformly in $(t,s)$: since $\{t<f\}\cap\{s<g\}$ factors as a measurable pair in the respective sub-$\sigma$-algebras, the integrand is exactly a super-level indicator covariance and `davydov_indicator_bound` gives $\le\alpha(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$. Verified, 0-axiom — the representation + uniform integrand bound that the bounded Davydov estimate integrates up.
mathContext: $\mathrm{Cov}(f,g)=\int_{(0,M]}\!\int_{(0,N]}\bigl(\mu\{t<f\wedge s<g\}-\mu\{t<f\}\mu\{s<g\}\bigr)ds\,dt$, with $|\text{integrand}|\le\alpha(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$ uniformly.

title: Bounded-variable Davydov estimate (S26/S27)
content: `bounded_covariance_le_alpha_mul_rectangle` integrates the uniform integrand bound over the rectangle: for $f\in[0,M]$ ($\sigma\mathrm{Pair}\,0$-measurable) and $g\in[0,N]$ ($\sigma\mathrm{Pair}\,1$-measurable), $|\mathrm{Cov}(f,g)|\le\alpha(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)\cdot M\cdot N$. The proof chains `covariance_eq_double_survival_covariance` and `survival_covariance_integrand_le_alpha` through `norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const` on the inner ($s$ over $(0,N]$, bound $\alpha N$) then outer ($t$ over $(0,M]$, bound $\alpha N M$) integral, using $\mathrm{vol}(Ioc\,0\,M)=M$. Its signed companion `signed_bounded_covariance_le_alpha_mul_rectangle` uses covariance translation-invariance to reduce a general $f\in[m,M]$, $g\in[n,N]$ to the nonnegative case, giving $|\mathrm{Cov}(f,g)|\le\alpha\,(M-m)(N-n)$. This is the bounded-variable base case of Davydov; the only remaining gap is lifting it to $L^p$ via truncation + Hölder. Verified, 0-axiom.
mathContext: $|\mathrm{Cov}(f,g)| \le \alpha(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)\,M\,N$ for $f\in[0,M],\,g\in[0,N]$; signed form $|\mathrm{Cov}(f,g)|\le\alpha\,(M-m)(N-n)$ for $f\in[m,M],\,g\in[n,N]$.

title: Davydov's covariance inequality (the L^p target, sorry)
content: `davydov_covariance_inequality` is the general $L^p$ bound (Davydov 1968) and one of the file's two remaining `sorry`s: for $X\in L^p(\mathcal F)$, $Y\in L^p(\mathcal G)$ with $p>2$, $|\mathrm{Cov}(X,Y)|\le 12\,\alpha(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)^{(p-2)/p}\|X\|_p\|Y\|_p$; the exponent $(p-2)/p$ specializes to $\delta/(2+\delta)$ at $p=2+\delta$, giving the Davydov–Ibragimov rate. The statement takes an arbitrary upper bound $\alpha_0\ge\alpha(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$ so the long-run-variance lemma can plug in the numerical bound directly. Its structural decomposition is *almost fully discharged* by this file: ingredients (1) `alphaMixingCoeff_le_one`, (2) `alphaMixingCoeff_nonneg`, and (3) `davydov_indicator_bound` are all proven, and the bounded-variable base case `signed_bounded_covariance_le_alpha_mul_rectangle` is in place; the only residue is ingredient (4), the $L^p$ density step (truncate $X,Y$ to bounded variables + Hölder amplification with conjugate exponents $(p, p/(p-1))$, references Doukhan 1994 §1.2.2, Bradley 2007 Thm 3.7). This `sorry` is the honest boundary between the verified infrastructure and the remaining ~100-line analytic step.
mathContext: $|\mathrm{Cov}(X,Y)| \le 12\,\alpha_0^{(p-2)/p}\,\|X\|_{L^p}\|Y\|_{L^p}$, with $\alpha(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)\le\alpha_0$ and $(p-2)/p = \delta/(2+\delta)$ at $p=2+\delta$.

title: Long-run variance absolute convergence (proven modulo Davydov)
content: `longrun_variance_absolutely_convergent` is the S5 deliverable — $\sum_k|\mathrm{Cov}(X_0,X_{k+1})|<\infty$ — and, crucially, a *fully verified chain modulo the single Davydov sorry*. The proof assembles the whole file: Davydov gives the per-term bound $|\mathrm{Cov}(X_0,X_{k+1})|\le 12\,\alpha(k+1)^{\delta/(2+\delta)}\|X_0\|_{2+\delta}\|X_{k+1}\|_{2+\delta}$; `stationary_eLpNorm_eq` collapses $\|X_{k+1}\|_{2+\delta}=\|X_0\|_{2+\delta}$ to a constant $M$; mean-zero simplifies the covariance to the raw integral; `polynomial_mixing_summable` (from `ibragimov_threshold_summable` after the $k\mapsto k+1$ shift) makes the envelope $K\sum_k\alpha(k+1)^{\delta/(2+\delta)}$ summable; and Mathlib's comparison test `Summable.of_nonneg_of_le` closes it. This is where the sharp threshold *pays off*: it is exactly the hypothesis that makes this series converge, hence that the long-run variance $\sigma^2=\mathrm{Var}(X_0)+2\sum_{k\ge1}\mathrm{Cov}(X_0,X_k)$ exists.
mathContext: $\sum_k \bigl|\int X_0\,X_{k+1}\,d\mu\bigr| \le K\sum_k \alpha(k+1)^{\delta/(2+\delta)} < \infty$, so $\sigma^2 = \mathrm{Var}(X_0)+2\sum_{k\ge1}\mathrm{Cov}(X_0,X_k)$ converges absolutely.

title: Ibragimov's CLT — the headline statement (sorry)
content: `mixing_clt_ibragimov` is the headline theorem and the file's second `sorry`: under `IbragimovHypotheses` and a positive long-run variance $\sigma^2>0$, the characteristic function of $S_n/\sqrt n$ converges pointwise to $\exp(-\sigma^2 t^2/2)$, the characteristic function of $\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)$; by Lévy's continuity theorem this is equivalent to $S_n/\sqrt n\to_d\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)$. The characteristic-function form (rather than a distribution-`Tendsto`) avoids Mathlib plumbing around Gaussian densities and `Measure.bind`, and $\sigma^2$ is passed as a parameter to decouple the S6+ proof from the S5 convergence step. The remaining proof is the classical Bernstein-block program: (S6) partition into large blocks of size $p_n$ separated by small gaps $q_n$ with $p_n\gg q_n\to\infty$; (S7) approximate large blocks by independent copies using $\alpha(q_n)\to 0$; (S8) verify Lindeberg's condition (consuming the $(2+\delta)$-moment bound and the truncation estimates of Part II-bis); (S9) invoke the Lindeberg–Feller CLT from the parent file. Estimated ~400 lines atop the Davydov/Bernstein infrastructure.
mathContext: $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\int_\Omega \exp\!\Bigl(it\cdot\tfrac{1}{\sqrt n}\sum_{k<n}X_k\Bigr)d\mu = \exp\!\Bigl(-\tfrac{\sigma^2 t^2}{2}\Bigr)\quad\forall t\in\mathbb R$.
